correctness.rationale: The incidence axioms give \(NN^{\mathsf T}=qI+J\) and \(N^{\mathsf T}N=qI+J-C\). Splitting the zero-sum hyperplane gives a \(q\)-dimensional parallel-class scalar, \(q^2-1\) identical two-by-two blocks, and one constant-population mode. At \(p_*=\log_2(q/(q-1))\), the parallel scalar vanishes, and convexity bounds \(1+3(a-1)/2\le3^{p_*}\le2a-1\) make the other blocks nonpositive, with order two checked separately. Above this endpoint a parallel-class witness is positive; Gaussian-kernel strict positivity below proves strictness and embedding ranks. The attached graph checker tests prime-field orders 2, 3, 5, and 7, but is not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The point--line graph metric of an arbitrary finite affine plane is a canonical geometric object with nontrivial parallel classes. An exact closed maximal negative-type exponent answers when its snowflake embeds isometrically into real Hilbert space and gives the precise affine-dimension drop at the threshold. Dependence only on the order, the exceptional order-two boundary, and the asymptotic \(1/(q\log2)\) make this a natural full-family metric invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
